findings.issue: The dependency graph contains a cycle, so the plan cannot be scheduled. T3's dependency on T2 is also semantically wrong: the snapshot derives from the migration, not the DTO.
findings.evidence: T1 after=[T3]; T3 after=[T2]; T2 after=[T1]. T3 is 'regenerate migration snapshot after DTO update', yet the baseline says the snapshot is 'derived repository metadata'. The requirements say all dependencies must be acyclic.
findings.failure_scenario: No valid topological order exists. A scheduler either deadlocks or rejects the plan, so the migration, DTO, snapshot and final verification never run. If the cycle is broken arbitrarily, the snapshot may be generated before the migration exists and miss delivery_note.
findings.fix: Remove T1's dependency on T3 so that T1 has no predecessors. Make T3 depend on T1 (the snapshot derives from the migration). Keep T2 after T1 only if it is needed, and keep T5 after T3 and T4.

findings.issue: T2 and T4 both write the same checked-in generated contract file. Both depend only on T1, so they can run in parallel, and no merge owner is named. The 'order-contract' resource label does not lock them. T4 also hand-patches a generated shared contract instead of consuming T2's output.
findings.evidence: T2 writes=[apps/api/order-dto.ts,packages/contracts/order.ts], resources=[order-contract]; T4 writes=[apps/web/order-client.ts,packages/contracts/order.ts], resources=[order-contract]; both after=[T1]; 'No merge owner exists.' Requirements: 'resource labels alone do not lock tasks' and 'both producer and consumer must compile against the same final definition'.
findings.failure_scenario: Concurrent edits to packages/contracts/order.ts overwrite each other or conflict. The API and web client can end up compiled against different Order definitions, for example with delivery_note typed or optional differently. T4's manual patch can also be erased by the next regeneration, so the contract drifts silently.
findings.fix: Make packages/contracts/order.ts owned solely by T2 (the producer) and remove it from T4's writes. Set T4 after=[T2] so the client serializer consumes the finalized contract. T4 should only edit apps/web/order-client.ts.

findings.issue: The verification command chains the checks with '&&', which short-circuits on the first failure. That contradicts both the requirement and T5's own acceptance criterion to run and record all three checks even if lint fails.
findings.evidence: command='npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit'; acceptance='record the exit status of all three checks, including if lint fails'. Requirements: 'Execute lint, typecheck and unit tests even if an earlier command fails, recording an exit status for each.'
findings.failure_scenario: If lint fails, typecheck and unit tests never run. There are then no exit statuses for them, the acceptance criterion cannot be met, and contract or type errors and test regressions in the delivery_note change go undetected.
findings.fix: Run the three commands independently and capture each status, for example `npm run lint; l=$?; npm run typecheck; t=$?; npm run test:unit; u=$?`. Write all three statuses to docs/run.md and exit non-zero if any is non-zero. Use a POSIX shell for this, since fish uses $status rather than $?.

uncertainties: The plan does not say whether the API/DTO change (T2) is deployed only after the migration (T1) is applied. Only 'migration deployment and frontend deployment' are mentioned as staged separately. If the API ships before the column exists and reads or writes delivery_note, existing order behavior could break. The baseline only guarantees that the migration is backward-compatible, not that the API tolerates a missing column.
